C1.quote: many of us were consciously making a longterm bet that principled control of effects would ultimately turn out to be important, despite the dominance of effects-by-default in mainstream languages.
C1.statement: Control effects on principle and make them explicit, even at the cost of convenience. (instead of: effects by default, unrestricted side effects)

C2.quote: the big advantage is conceptual. It is much easier to think abstractly in terms of computations than concretely in terms of the details of failure and success continuations.
C2.statement: Capture any notion of computation as an abstract value you sequence, rather than wiring each effect into the language. (instead of: a single built-in notion of computation and sequencing)

C3.quote: They were originally proposed early in the design process, by Wadler and Blott ... as a ... principled solution to a relatively small problem (operator overloading for numeric operations and equality).
C3.statement: Solve overloading with one principled general mechanism, constraints on types, rather than ad hoc special cases. (instead of: ad hoc operator overloading)

C4.quote: Because of referential transparency, Haskell programs can be viewed as executable mathematics, as equations over the category of complete partial orders. In principle, at least, the specification becomes the program.
C4.statement: Keep the language referentially transparent so programs read as executable mathematics. (instead of: programs as sequences of state changes)

C5.quote: The Haskell Committee wanted expressions to look as much like mathematics as possible, and thus from day one we bought into the idea that Haskell would have infix operators.
C5.statement: Make notation follow mathematical usage and the reader's eye. (instead of: the syntactic tradition of other programming languages)

C6.quote: solutions that feel like minimal surfaces: simple expressions that comprise significant complexity, with forms that seem natural, recurring in problem after problem
C6.statement: Prefer the simplest expression that carries the complexity, the form that recurs naturally across problems. (instead of: bespoke machinery built per problem)

C7.quote: we intended the language to be quite conservative, rather than to break new ground
C7.statement: Embody tried-and-true consensus rather than break new ground. (instead of: including novel, unproven features)
